## 1. Lattices & semilattices

#### [DEF] lattice — Lattice / semilattice
**Statement.** A poset is a meet- (resp. join-) semilattice if every pair of elements has a greatest lower bound x∧y (resp. least upper bound x∨y); a lattice if it is both. The operations are associative, commutative, idempotent, and absorptive.
**Status.** Definition. Sources: [DP02].
**In this repo.** `IsMeetSemilattice`, `IsJoinSemilattice`, `IsLattice` — `posets/LatticeClasses.v`; order/operation bridges in `posets/LatticeOrder.v`.

#### [DEF] complete-lattice — Complete lattice
**Statement.** A lattice in which every subset (not just every pair) has both a meet and a join; in particular it has a least element ⊥ and greatest element ⊤.
**Status.** Definition. Sources: [DP02].
**Depends on.** [lattice]

#### [THM] birkhoff-representation — Birkhoff's representation theorem
**Statement.** Every finite distributive lattice L is isomorphic to the lattice of down-sets (order ideals) of its poset of join-irreducible elements, ordered by inclusion. Finite distributive lattices and finite posets are thus dual notions.
**Status.** Proven (Birkhoff 1937). Sources: [Birkhoff37]; [DP02].
**Depends on.** [lattice]
**Notes.** The fundamental duality behind [distributive-lattice-dim] in the dimension index.

#### [THM] distributive-modular-forbidden — M3/N5 sublattice test
**Statement.** A lattice is distributive iff it contains neither M3 (the diamond) nor N5 (the pentagon) as a sublattice; it is modular iff it contains no N5.
**Status.** Proven (Dedekind; Birkhoff). Sources: [Birkhoff67]; [DP02].
**Depends on.** [lattice]

#### [THM] pudlak-tuma — Universality of partition lattices
**Statement.** Every finite lattice is isomorphic to a sublattice of a finite partition lattice (Pudlák–Tůma 1980).
**Status.** Proven (Pudlák–Tůma 1980). Sources: [PT80].
**Depends on.** [lattice]

## 2. Chains, antichains & extremal set theory

Dilworth's and Mirsky's theorems live in the dimension index (`dimension-index.md` §2); this section collects the extremal-set and refinement results.

#### [THM] sperner — Sperner's theorem
**Statement.** The largest antichain in the Boolean lattice 2^[n] (subsets ordered by inclusion) has size C(n, ⌊n/2⌋), achieved by the middle layer.
**Status.** Proven (Sperner 1928). Sources: [Sperner28]; [DP02].

#### [THM] lym — LYM inequality
**Statement.** For any antichain A in 2^[n], Σ_{S ∈ A} 1 / C(n, |S|) ≤ 1 (Lubell–Yamamoto–Meshalkin). This refines and implies Sperner's theorem.
**Status.** Proven (Lubell 1966 and independently). Sources: [Lubell66].
**Depends on.** [sperner]

#### [THM] greene-kleitman — Greene–Kleitman theorem
**Statement.** For each k, the maximum size of a union of k antichains of a finite poset equals min over chain partitions C of Σ_{C} min(|C|, k); dually for unions of k chains versus antichain partitions. For k = 1 these recover Mirsky's and Dilworth's theorems.
**Status.** Proven (Greene–Kleitman 1976). Sources: [GK76]; [DP02].
**Notes.** The common refinement of the two classical chain/antichain covering theorems.

## 3. Fixed-point theory

#### [DEF] dcpo — Directed-complete partial order (dcpo / CPO)
**Statement.** A poset in which every directed subset has a supremum is a dcpo; a *pointed* dcpo additionally has a least element ⊥. The foundation of denotational semantics.
**Status.** Definition. Sources: [DP02].

#### [THM] knaster-tarski — Knaster–Tarski fixed-point theorem
**Statement.** Every monotone (order-preserving) map f on a complete lattice L has a fixed point; moreover the set of fixed points of f is itself a complete lattice (in particular f has a least and a greatest fixed point).
**Status.** Proven (Knaster–Tarski; Tarski 1955). Sources: [Tarski55]; [DP02].
**Depends on.** [complete-lattice]
**Notes.** Underpins inductive/coinductive definitions and program semantics.

#### [THM] kleene-fixpoint — Kleene fixed-point theorem
**Statement.** On a pointed dcpo, a Scott-continuous map f has least fixed point ⊔_{n≥0} f^n(⊥) — the supremum of the ascending Kleene chain.
**Status.** Proven (Kleene). Sources: [DP02].
**Depends on.** [dcpo], [knaster-tarski]

## 4. Well-quasi-orders & well-foundedness

#### [DEF] wqo — Well-quasi-order
**Statement.** A quasi-order Q is a well-quasi-order (wqo) if it has no infinite strictly descending chain and no infinite antichain; equivalently, every infinite sequence x₁, x₂, … has indices i < j with x_i ≤ x_j.
**Status.** Definition. Sources: [DP02].

#### [THM] dickson — Dickson's lemma
**Statement.** (ℕ^k, ≤) with the componentwise order is a well-quasi-order; equivalently every subset of ℕ^k has finitely many minimal elements.
**Status.** Proven (Dickson 1913). Sources: [Dickson13].
**Depends on.** [wqo]
**Notes.** Guarantees termination of many algorithms (e.g. Gröbner-basis / monomial-ideal arguments).

#### [THM] higman — Higman's lemma
**Statement.** If Q is a well-quasi-order then the set Q* of finite sequences over Q, ordered by the subsequence-embedding order, is also a well-quasi-order.
**Status.** Proven (Higman 1952). Sources: [Higman52].
**Depends on.** [wqo]

#### [THM] kruskal-tree — Kruskal's tree theorem
**Statement.** The set of finite trees, ordered by topological-minor (homeomorphic) embedding, is a well-quasi-order (Kruskal 1960).
**Status.** Proven (Kruskal 1960). Sources: [Kruskal60].
**Depends on.** [wqo], [higman]

## 5. Incidence algebra & Möbius functions

#### [DEF] mobius-function — Möbius function of a poset
**Statement.** For a locally finite poset, the Möbius function μ is the inverse of the zeta function in the incidence algebra: μ(x,x) = 1 and Σ_{x ≤ z ≤ y} μ(x,z) = 0 for all x < y.
**Status.** Definition (Rota 1964). Sources: [Rota64]; [DP02].

#### [THM] mobius-inversion — Möbius inversion formula
**Statement.** If g(x) = Σ_{y ≤ x} f(y) for all x in a locally finite poset, then f(x) = Σ_{y ≤ x} μ(y, x) g(y). This unifies inclusion–exclusion (Boolean lattice) and classical number-theoretic Möbius inversion (divisibility lattice).
**Status.** Proven (Rota 1964). Sources: [Rota64].
**Depends on.** [mobius-function]

## 6. Galois connections & closure operators

#### [DEF] galois-connection — Galois connection
**Statement.** An (antitone) Galois connection between posets P and Q is a pair of maps f: P → Q, g: Q → P with y ≤_Q f(x) ⇔ x ≤_P g(y). Then g∘f and f∘g are closure operators, and f, g restrict to a dual isomorphism between the closed sets.
**Status.** Definition (Ore 1944). Sources: [Ore44]; [DP02].

#### [THM] closure-fixpoints-lattice — Closed sets form a complete lattice
**Statement.** The fixed points (closed elements) of a closure operator on a complete lattice form a complete lattice. (Instances: the Dedekind–MacNeille completion, and the concept lattice of formal concept analysis.)
**Status.** Proven. Sources: [DP02].
**Depends on.** [galois-connection], [complete-lattice]

## 7. In this repo — formalized order-theory results

#### [FACT] hb-not-semilattice — Happened-before is not a semilattice
**Statement.** The happened-before causal order of a distributed execution cannot, in general, carry a meet- or join-semilattice structure compatible with it — there is no canonical greatest common cause / least common effect.
**Status.** Proven (this repository). Sources: [DP02].
**Depends on.** [lattice]
**In this repo.** `happened_before_not_join_semilattice_poset` and companions — `happenedBefore/SemilatticeContradiction.v` (see `happenedBefore/README.md`).

#### [FACT] crdt-join-semilattice — CRDT convergence via join-semilattices
**Statement.** State-based CRDTs converge (strong eventual consistency) because replica states form a join-semilattice and the merge operation is the join: merges are commutative, associative, and idempotent, so replicas that have seen the same updates reach the same least upper bound.
**Status.** Proven (this repository). Sources: [DP02].
**Depends on.** [lattice]
**In this repo.** `strong_eventual_consistency` — `eventualConsistency/crdts/StateBased.v`; convergence development in `eventualConsistency/ConvergenceProof.v`.

#### [THM] hall-marriage — Hall's marriage theorem
**Statement.** A bipartite graph has a perfect matching saturating one side iff Hall's condition holds: every subset X of that side has |N(X)| ≥ |X|.
**Status.** Proven (this repository). Sources: [DP02].
**In this repo.** `hall_marriage_theorem` — `posets/dilworth/Hall.v`; used to prove Dilworth's theorem (`posets/dilworth/DilworthTheorem.v`).
